title: Add deterministic combat regression fixture for first combat playtest
description:
Create a regression-style scripted or semi-scripted test based on the first combat playtest. Do not depend on the natural RNG stream causing Bob to drop to 0 HP. Instead, use a deterministic roll fixture / fake roll tool / roll-plan mode for exact mechanical-path tests, and keep live RNG playtest recipes branch-tolerant.

Acceptance criteria:

- Provide a deterministic combat fixture that can force Bob wins initiative; Bob's first attack misses; goblin attacks miss; Bob's second attack hits; Bob's damage kills `goblin-1`; `goblin-2` critically hits Bob; damage drops Bob to 0 HP; Bob makes a death save and succeeds.
- Assert mechanical invariants rather than exact prose: rolls are executed by tools; player-visible rolls are surfaced according to policy; HP changes are state-backed; combatant ids are stable once combatant state exists; rejected candidates do not persist state; successful retries do not duplicate state writes.
- Include a live playtest recipe using real RNG, but make it branch-tolerant: if Bob attacks, player attack roll is visible; if Bob hits, damage roll is visible; if a goblin attacks Bob, attack roll is visible; if Bob takes damage, damage and HP/state change are visible; if Bob reaches 0 HP, unconscious/dying state and death-save flow are visible; if Bob kills both goblins, combat ends cleanly and state reflects both enemies defeated.
- Mark any parts blocked on the combatant-state bead.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic first-combat regression fixture, rollback/retry invariants, and branch-tolerant live RNG playtest recipe. PR #305.
